body:
Vape prices vary widely, from a few dollars for a small device to well over a hundred for a kit or a bulk pack, and the sticker price on its own tells you very little about value. A $25 device can cost less per puff than a $13 one, a $12 bottle can be cheaper per day than a $20 one and a kit that looks expensive can be the cheapest way to vape over a year. This guide gives you a simple method for comparing any vape product fairly: cost per puff for disposables, cost per milliliter and per day for liquid, running cost for kits, how to include shipping and discounts and how to avoid false economy. It is written for adults aged 21 and over. Nicotine is addictive, and nothing here is advice to use more.

## The three numbers
These three numbers make it easy to compare almost anything.

### Cost per puff (disposables)
Divide the price by the stated puff count. Because the result is tiny, it is easier to compare per 1,000 puffs. A $17.99 device rated at 30,000 puffs costs about $0.60 per 1,000 puffs. A $12.99 device rated at 5,000 puffs costs about $2.60 per 1,000 puffs, more than four times as much per puff. Puff counts are manufacturer estimates, so use them to compare devices, not to predict exact life. See [puff counts explained](/blog/puff-count-explained/).

### Cost per mL (e-liquid)
Divide the price by the bottle size. Larger bottles are cheaper per mL, but salts are consumed slowly because of their strength, so a 30 mL bottle may last as long as a larger freebase bottle. A 30 mL bottle at $12 is $0.40 per mL, and a 100 mL at $15 is $0.15 per mL. See [e-liquid bottle sizes](/blog/e-liquid-bottle-sizes-30ml-60ml-100ml/).

### Cost per day (everything)
Multiply by how much you use. If you use 1.5 mL of salts a day, a $12 bottle of 30 mL costs $0.60 a day. If you take 400 puffs a day, a device at $0.60 per 1,000 puffs costs $0.24 a day. Cost per day is the fairest comparison across product types.

## Running cost (kits)
For a refillable kit, add up the device, the liquid you will use per week and the replacement coils or pods. A kit often costs more up front but less per month than disposables. Suppose a pod kit costs $25, liquid costs $12 a month and coils cost $6 a month. Over six months, that is $25 plus $108, so $133, or about $22 a month. If disposables cost you $27 a month, six months cost $162. The kit saves about $29 in that period, and more as time passes. Run the numbers for your own use.

## Check what is included
A multi-pack, free shipping threshold or crypto and gift card discount can change the total. We offer a 10% discount for crypto and gift card payments, and free shipping on orders of $200 or more after discount, with a flat $15 fee below that. The minimum order is $100. See [the 10% crypto and gift card discount](/blog/crypto-discount-how-it-works/) and [minimum order and free shipping explained](/blog/minimum-order-and-free-shipping-explained/). Include shipping in the cost, because a cheap device with expensive shipping may not be cheap.

## Include everything
When you compare, include: the device, liquid or pods, coils, charging accessories, shipping, tax where it applies and any discount. Leave out things you will buy whatever you choose. See [vape taxes by state](/blog/vape-taxes-by-state-overview/) for how tax can change the total.

## Beware false economy
The cheapest device is not a bargain if it fails early. Look at product details and brand reputation in our [disposable vapes](/shop/disposables/) listings before you decide. A device with a weak battery may stop before the liquid ends. A device with a poor coil may lose flavor early. A very low price may signal old or counterfeit stock; see [how to spot counterfeit vapes](/blog/how-to-spot-counterfeit-vapes/).

## A quick example
Two items at $18 and $24 look far apart, but if the second lasts three times longer, it costs less per puff. Always compare the full picture. If the $18 device has 8,000 puffs ($2.25 per 1,000) and the $24 device has 24,000 puffs ($1.00 per 1,000), the second costs less than half as much per puff. If you will not use 24,000 puffs, the comparison changes, so think about your use.

## Comparing different product types
How do you compare a disposable with a pod kit, or with pouches? Use cost per day. Work out how many puffs, how many milliliters or how many pouches you use per day, multiply by the unit cost and add the fixed costs spread over time. Our guide to [nicotine pouches](/blog/how-many-pouches-in-a-can-and-how-long-it-lasts/) shows the same method for cans. The aim is a single number in dollars per day.

## A worked table in words
- **Disposable, 30,000 puffs at $17.99, 400 puffs a day:** about $0.24 a day.
- **Pod kit, liquid and coils at about $18 a month:** about $0.60 a day, plus the kit cost spread over months.
- **Sub-ohm tank, 8 mL a day of a $15 100 mL bottle, plus coils:** about $1.20 a day for liquid plus about $0.30 for coils.
- **Nicotine pouches, 5 a day at $0.30 each:** $1.50 a day.

These are example numbers only. Your own use and the prices you pay decide the real figures.

## Common mistakes
- **Comparing sticker prices only.**
- **Forgetting shipping and tax.**
- **Assuming a bigger device is always better value.**
- **Ignoring your own use.**
- **Trusting very low prices.**

## Frequently asked questions in depth
### Are puff counts accurate?
They are estimates. Real life varies, but they work for comparing devices.

### How do I count my puffs?
Estimate for a week. A rough count is enough.

### Does shipping change the comparison?
Yes. Free shipping above $200 after discount can lower the effective price of bigger orders.

### Is the discount worth planning around?
For larger orders, yes. A 10% saving can be significant.

### How do I compare a kit with disposables?
Use cost per month, including the kit cost spread over the months you will use it.

## Shop
Browse [disposable vapes](/shop/disposables/) and [vape juice](/shop/vape-juice/). All products are for adults aged 21 and over, and nicotine is addictive.

## A step-by-step comparison method
1. Write down the products you are considering, with prices.
2. For disposables, write the puff count, then divide price by puffs in thousands.
3. For liquids, write the volume, then divide price by milliliters.
4. For kits, list the device, a month of liquid and a month of coils or pods.
5. Estimate your daily use, and multiply to get cost per day.
6. Add shipping or subtract any discount that applies to your order.
7. Compare the final numbers, then think about flavor, brand and features.

This takes ten minutes, and it replaces guesswork with figures you can trust.

## A longer worked example
You are choosing between three disposables. Device A is 6,000 puffs at $13.99, Device B is 25,000 puffs at $17.99 and Device C is 50,000 puffs at $19.99. Cost per 1,000 puffs is about $2.33 for A, $0.72 for B and $0.40 for C. You take about 300 puffs a day. A lasts 20 days, costing $0.70 a day. B lasts 83 days, costing $0.22 a day. C lasts 167 days, costing $0.12 a day. C is cheapest per day, but only if you will still enjoy the same device after five and a half months. B may be the sensible middle. A suits a trial. The numbers help, and your own judgment completes the decision.

## Where price comparisons mislead
Prices can mislead when puff counts are exaggerated, when batteries are weak, when flavors fade early or when shipping and tax are ignored. A device with a very high puff count and a tiny battery may not deliver what it says. Read reviews, check the battery and the charging port and compare several devices of similar size.

## Tracking your spending
Keep a simple record of what you buy and how long it lasts. After a couple of months you will know your real cost per day, and you can compare it with alternatives. Many people are surprised by how much they spend, or by how much they could save. The numbers are yours to use as you see fit.

## Frequently asked questions about price comparison
### Should I trust the puff count on a very cheap device?
Be cautious. A very cheap device with a very high puff count may not deliver it, and it may be old or counterfeit stock. Compare with similar devices, and check the battery.

### Does a higher price mean better quality?
Not necessarily. Price reflects capacity, features and brand as well as quality. Compare the full picture.

### How often do prices change?
Regularly, with promotions and stock. Check the product page before you order.
